## Why 东区 is the better performer — and what tempers it

- 东区 leads on both sides of the equation: the highest June collections (¥49,350.50, ~45% of the total) and the largest absolute refund outflow (¥8,600.50), still netting ¥7,850 more than 西区.
- The lead is concentrated, not broad: ¥35,000 of 东区's ¥49,350.50 comes from two orders (O02 ¥20,000 and O07 ¥15,000). It is a large-ticket story rather than a unique strength across many stores.
- 北区 looks efficient (no June refunds, ¥22,000 pulled from only two real orders of ¥11,000 each, plus one ¥0 order). That is high average value but thinly supported — a repeat month would likely look very different.
- 南区 is negative purely because it booked no June sales but absorbed a ¥1,200 refund against an April order (O15). That is a timing artifact, not operational deterioration in the month.

## Data handling that affects the conclusion

1. **Duplicate business records counted once.** O12 (¥2,000, 东区) appeared twice in the export and refund R09 (¥100, 东区) appeared twice; each is counted once. Counting the duplicates would have overstated 东区's net by ¥1,900 (and would wrongly book a phantom refund).
2. **Different IDs with identical date/amount are treated as separate transactions.** O13 and O14 are both 北区, 2026-06-09, ¥11,000, and R16/R17 are both ¥100 against order O22 on the same day. Per your rule they all count. This is the single biggest swing factor: if O13/O14 were actually one duplicated sale, 北区 would drop to ¥11,000 and change its standing versus 西区 materially. **Worth confirming with the source system.**
3. **Refunds are dated by when the refund happened, not by the original order month.** Two June refunds relate to older orders: R03 ¥2,000 (order O08 from May 31 → hits 西区) and R12 ¥1,200 (order O15 from April 30 → the only item in 南区). Conversely, refund R18 on order O18 was booked May 31 and is excluded from June.
4. **Cancelled orders earn nothing.** O10 (¥3,000, 东区) and O20 (¥2,700, 南区), both dated in June, are excluded. Including them would have lifted 东区 to ¥43,750 — the ranking does not change, but the level does.
5. **Boundary dates kept inclusive.** June 1 and June 30 items are in (O01, R12, O02 paid 6/30, R07/R09/R15 refunds on 6/30); the neighbours are out (O08 paid 5/31 with its 5/31 refund R08, O09 paid 7/1, O19 paid 7/2, and order O02's July 3 refund R02 of ¥3,000).
6. **Region comes from the store table, not the order file.** All 8 stores map to the 4 regions, and 北区 is defined by a single store (S05). All four regions are shown even where there is no June activity, which is why 南区 appears at ¥-1,200.

## One forward-looking caveat

Order O02 (东区, ¥20,000) has a ¥3,000 refund dated 2026-07-03 — outside June, so it does not reduce June's ¥40,750. It will land in July's settlement, so 东区 starts next month ¥3,000 in the hole. Scope of this analysis is the single 25-order / 17-refund file; the comparisons describe this file only.

## What changed, region by region

Only two regions moved, and only three of the five new records had any June effect:

| Refund | Region | What happened | June impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| **R10** (new) | 东区 | Previously unrecorded refund of ¥9,000 on order O02, dated 2026-06-30 | **-9,000** |
| **R07** (corrected) | 东区 | Amount raised from ¥7,000 to ¥9,000, same order/date | **-2,000** |
| **R12** (corrected) | 南区 | Amount reduced from ¥1,200 to ¥900, same order/date | **+300** |
| R11 (new) | 西区 | ¥500 refund on order O05 dated **2026-07-01** | none (July) |
| R19 (new) | 北区 | ¥500 refund on order O13 dated **2026-07-02** | none (July) |

- **东区: -11,000** — both hits land in June and both hit the same order family. Order O02 (¥20,000, the region's largest order) was already carrying a ¥3,000 refund dated 2026-07-03; the newly registered R10 adds a further ¥9,000 refunded on 2026-06-30. O02 is now **60% refunded (¥12,000 of ¥20,000)**.
- **西区: unchanged.** Its new item (R11) is dated July 1, so by the "refund by date incurred" rule it belongs to next month. 西区 therefore keeps the best-in-class refund ratio: 11.8% of collections, versus 东区's 39.7%.
- **北区: unchanged in June**, but note that R19 is the region's **first refund ever** — 北区's clean record in the June table is coincidental timing, and July will show ¥500.
- **南区: improved by 300**, purely because its only June item (a refund on an April order) was corrected downward. It remains negative since the region booked no June sales.

## Does the conclusion change?

**Yes — the winner changes, and it is not a close call relative to rounding:** 西区 now leads 东区 by ¥3,150, whereas the previous version had 东区 ahead by ¥7,850. This is a genuine re-ranking driven by one newly registered large refund, not a rounding or presentation effect.

The qualitative read also shifts: on collections alone 东区 is still the biggest region, but after refunds it is the **most refund-eroded**, and its lead depends heavily on O02 — an order that has now been refunded twice on two different dates. 西区 is the better settlement performer because it converts collections to net cash more efficiently.

## Caveats worth checking

- **O02's two refunds (¥9,000 in June + ¥3,000 in July) should be confirmed as two separate real events** rather than a re-registration of one event under a new ID (R10 vs R02). If they are in fact one event, 东区's June refund is ¥9,000 too high and 东区 would return to roughly ¥38,750 — in which case 东区 would lead again. This is the single item that decides the ranking.
- My earlier flag on **O13/O14** (北区, identical ¥11,000 on 2026-06-09) is partly, but not fully, resolved: R19 refunds against O13 specifically, which suggests O13 is a real separate order. Still worth a source-system check, since ¥11,000 of 北区's ¥22,000 sits on it.
- Unchanged from before: cancelled orders earn nothing (O10 ¥3,000 东区, O20 ¥2,700 南区 excluded), and duplicate export rows are counted once (O12 order, R09 refund). The O12/R09 dedupe no longer affects any ranking question now that O12's refund and O02's are in play.
- All figures describe this file set only; with 4 regions and 16 June orders, per-region results are sensitive to single large transactions.
